title: First Chicago job and the Dreamland band with Louis
summary: Miss Major sent for Joe, who took Johnny St. Cyr, Jimmy Noone and the Dodds brothers, with Dutrey, to Chicago. Joe and Louis played together at the Dreamland and Royal Garden.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Do you remember his very first job? Was it the Royal Garden or do you remember the Dreamland?

Was he there? Oh that was in Chicago. In Chicago, I thought I meant. And then he worked at the Pekin. That was after hours for all the actress and actress. They worked at 6 o'clock in the morning. After everything was over, all the actress and actresses, big name, would come to the Pekins.
How did he get the first job in Chicago? Did he go up and look around or did somebody

send for him? No, Miss Major sent for him. Sent for him. He got the job for him. She sent for him and he had in his band, he carried for me, Jonathan Sear, a banjo player. Jimmy Noon, a clarinet player. And the two Dodge brothers, they left here with him to go to Chicago to play his first job in Chicago.
And, uh, what's the other one? It was the trombone. Nora Dutrie. Nora Dutrie. I know he made some records with him.

Yes. And, um, well they had quite a nice band up there. They went over there. It was a great band. Yes, it was. Because all the, uh, all the downtown big folks used to come to the Dreamland, to the Royal Garden to hear Joe play. Him and Louie then were playing together. Mm-hmm. And they used to make what they called then bricks. Yes. When Louie would make a brick, Joe would catch it just like that. And it was the prettiest thing. I wished I had some records.
I have those records. I've heard them. They're beautiful. Beautiful music.
